annotations.title: A Prieſt for euer.
annotations.text: In two reſpectes Chriſt is a Prieſt for euer: ◦ in that from the firſt inſtant of his Incarnation he was, and remaneth a Prieſt, now alſo in heauen: and al other Prieſtes are his miniſterial vicares, not ſucceſſors. So that al prieſtly functions, which they doe, he by them doth the ſame, as the principal Prieſt. Wherupon ſaith S. Paul ( 1. Cor 4. ) So let a man thincke of vs, as of the miniſters of Chriſt, and diſpenſers of the myſteries of God. Secondly Chriſt dayly offering Sacrifice by the handes of his Prieſtes, doth continually pacifie Gods wrath, in behalf of thoſe ſinners, for whom it is duly applied, euen to the end of the world. Wheras the Prieſthood of Aaron, and of al others in the old Teſtament, ceaſſed by their deathes, both in the office, and in the effect.

notes.text: Christs Priesthood for euer both in function and in effect.

annotations.title: According to the order of Melchiſedech.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> As Melchiſedech, king of peace and iuſtice, without father, mother, or genealogie, expreſſed in holie Scriptures, or otherwiſe knowen to the world, was Prieſt of the Hiegheſt, offered bread and wine, an vnbloudie ſacrifice; communicating with both Chananeites and Hebrewes, bleſſed Abraham, and tooke tithes of him and his ſubiectes: ſo Chriſt the true King of peace & iuſtice, without father of his humanity, without mother of his Diuinitie, the Sonne of God, of ineffable genealogie, borne of a virgin in his humanitie, the Prieſt of God, offereth Sacrifice ( not only bloudie on the Croſſe, but alſo ) vnbloudie in the formes of bread and wine, continueth the ſame by the miniſterie of other Prieſtes, maketh al nations parrakers therof, bleſſeth them and receiueth of them al dutiful and religious ſeruice, as of his ſubiectes.

notes.text: The resemblance of Christs and Melchisedecs Priesthood.
